Dear Sumi,

Here is a collection of things we noticed about how you dress, what you love wearing and where we think we can make getting dressed a little easier.

Warmly,

Reading you

Your style

Comfort, ease and a little bit of unexpected.

You have a good sense of what you like to live in. Your wardrobe is edited, with a handful of pieces you return to often. You gravitate towards clothes that feel comfortable and easy, with classic silhouettes that you know work for you. But you also enjoy doing things a little differently. You have a distinct way of bringing your personality into the way you dress. Whether it's through the T-shirts you design yourself or the different ways you find to wear a piece, you seem to enjoy making clothes feel personal to you.

Your Oddly wardrobe

Trisha
in Sand

You have a lovely instinct for making a piece your own. You've worn Trisha around seven times, styling it with your Pashmina shawl and even wearing it almost like a salwar with leggings. You seem to approach clothes with a sense of curiosity, finding ways to wear a piece that feel natural to you.

What we believe

The pieces you love the most, you should be able to wear the most.

So here are three more ways to wear Trisha.

Ideas, not instructions

Swap in whatever in your wardrobe you're genuinely excited about right now.

Trisha, way one

For this
festive season

Swipe a piece to see it closer

Three ways to wear Trisha
  1. 01

    Worn long over the olive silk, like a kurta. Sand and olive together feel rich without trying too hard.

  2. 02

    Let gold do the work: the crescent earrings, the bangle, and nothing at the neck so the embroidery gets the attention.

  3. 03

    When the puja turns into a party, swap your flats for the gold heels and take the small clutch.

Trisha, way two

For a quick fix

Three ways to wear Trisha
  1. 01

    On its own with the Mary Janes. The burgundy adds a little warmth to the sand.

  2. 02

    Keep jewellery quiet: the silver watch and the tiny studs, nothing more.

  3. 03

    Throw the slouchy bag over your shoulder and go, from errands to lunch without a second thought.

Trisha, way three

For your next

Three ways to wear Trisha
  1. 01

    The blush mules and the cream bag keep things soft, light and tonal.

  2. 02

    Pick one pair of earrings: warm gold while it's still light out, the diamond drops once the evening starts.

  3. 03

    Bring your Pashmina for when it gets cooler. You already know that pairing works.

Your go-tos

What you
reach for

You have a small group of brands you return to for occasions, including Bagh and Anokhi. When you're unsure what others might wear, Oddly becomes an easy choice because you know you'll feel well dressed without feeling overdressed.

For you, we think the sweet spot is:
Comfortable + elevated + distinctive

Your upcoming occasions
  1. 01

    Diwali

    You tend towards reds, oranges, yellows and greens be it for pujas during the day or a Diwali party with your loved ones.

  2. 02

    Karva Chauth

    You traditionally wear something from your mother or grandmother, either a saree or a dupatta made into a suit. You shared that clothes are emotions to you.

  3. 03

    Travel

    Shorts and T-shirts are your easy go-to on vacation. Packing under 30 minutes seems to be your super power!

Finishing touch

Your hair

You wear it down most days, natural or lightly styled, and that's exactly right — no need to change what already works. For the days you want it to feel a touch more done, without redoing the whole thing, here are some options:

  • Vacation, shorts & a t-shirt

    Down, natural, and low effort. This one doesn't need help.

  • Diwali, kurta with a neckpiece

    Down, front pieces pulled back with one clip. Same hair, ten extra seconds.

  • Karva Chauth, saree or dupatta from your mother or grandmother

    A loose, low bun, pulled apart a little so it doesn't look too neat.

A bun is also the easiest place to add a little more — a few fresh flowers or a small hair accessory tucked in instantly elevates it, no extra effort required.
